truth.rule: served.json: GET / 200 with the editor's title; GET /api/project 200 says a hike post is loaded (kind post), names a hike clip id of the tree's index and is served from this run's tree; the answer names 127.0.0.1/localhost with the served port; HEAD is the base, no tracked change (bytecode aside)

served.why_api: measured (moto_facts.json): /api/project says the LOADED edit's kind ('post' for a hike carousel, 'reel' for the default manifest_v4), its project.root and the hike clip ids, all inside the first 4 KB the driver keeps; /api/finds answers 409 on a reel and 200 on a post but names no root

scenarios.actions_target_why: 2 presses on a fresh folder, read from the build under test (merge-sas 69cf260): the clone has no servers.json and nirvanad/servers/detect.py finds no app (it reads top-level *.py for a top-level `= FastAPI(`; the editor builds its app inside build_app() in editor/server/main.py), so the Agent's do_here takes the HERE path of nirvanad/agent/here.py: here_trust [Allow] (trust once per folder, 'also in auto mode'), then here_save [Run it], one press that writes the personal row and starts the server with the trust key it answers. A worker-kept server instead raises one server_trust [Run it] (nirvanad/agent/trust_card.py; decision 0041 R4): 1 press, inside this target. The owner's rule -- trust is asked once per folder and command, even in auto mode -- makes these the presses a real user makes on a new folder; the bench's scratch home trusts nothing, so every run is a new folder. Claude Code's arm has no equivalent press (it runs under --dangerously-skip-permissions), so its actions stay 0 and the difference is the trust rule's cost, measured, not a defect.
scenarios.wall_target_why: Claude Code Sonnet 5.5 served it in 49 s on the owner's folder (decision 0041 §1)

claude_code.why: MEASURED 2026-10-18 (haiku, print mode, the owner's settings): Bash ran, Write was denied with 'haven't granted it yet'; with --permission-mode auto both ran. Arm N's pane starts in auto mode ('auto mode on' on its screen), so arm C gets the same posture for the scenarios that write or serve. M1 keeps the brief's argv unchanged.

scenarios.trust_why: the ask needs no running server, so actions_target stays 0; but a build worker that starts the editor to try its route and keeps it listening raises a server_trust card at turn end (decision 0041 R4), which the written card policy never presses: the run would stall to its 3600 s wall. Pressing it ends the stall, and each press still counts as a person action over the target, so the meter shows what the worker's choice cost.
